method: Built-in image_gen; native pixel sprite preparation and material palette separation offline.

models.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: an authentic low-resolution pixel-art car sprite for an Italian automotive browser RPG set around 2002 with a Windows 98 / early web visual language.
Create ONE complete isolated car on a genuinely transparent background, full car visible, front-left three-quarter view with nose pointing toward the bottom-left, approximately 40% front and 60% side, low eye-level camera with a little bonnet visible, straight wheels. Wide landscape canvas about 3:1. The car fills most of the width with clean transparent margins. No other cars, background, road, person, frames, caption or watermark.
Pixel art constructed on a logical approximately 320 x 128 pixel grid: crisp square pixels, deliberate one-pixel stair-step silhouettes and one-pixel dark panel gaps, limited 1990s racing-game palette, hand-drawn readable forms and modest 3-to-6-shade clusters. No photographic rendering, blurry antialiasing, 3D render, continuous gradients, smooth vector illustration, noisy dithering, chibi proportions or excessive gloss.
IMPORTANT RECOLOURABLE MATERIALS: use six distinctly GREEN shades ONLY for all painted body panels, painted bumpers, mirrors, skirts and wheel-arch lips, including all edge pixels. Suggested body ramp #103b24 #196137 #2f8a46 #4dac5a #80c773 #b4e89c. Keep even painted highlight pixels pale green, not pure white. Do not use green anywhere else. Window glass is dark STEEL BLUE and cool grey, tyres/rubber/grille/panel gaps charcoal or black, wheels silver grey, headlamps ivory and indicators amber. No green brake calipers or green reflections on other materials. This is a legitimate green paint option, with clean material separation for later palette swaps. Preserve genuine model identity and stock proportions.
The attached existing game image is a reference for model identity only: redraw it as coherent genuine pixel art, not a pixelation filter on a photograph.
Subject: a stock European Fiat Punto GT first generation Tipo 176, approximately 1995, THREE-DOOR compact hatchback, period correct. Faithful rounded Giugiaro shape, short sloping bonnet, wide rectangular slightly rounded headlamp units, slim upper grille with small period Fiat emblem, factory sporty body-coloured front bumper with dark horizontal intake and two small fog lights, black horizontal rubbing strip along sides, a single long side door and rear quarter window, thick rear pillar and tall vertical rear light, small original silver five-spoke alloy wheels, normal road-car ride height. Not a later Punto generation, not a five-door, not an Abarth body kit, no modern LED lamps, no racing decals, no oversized wheels. Small European period licence plate with non-readable pixel marks. Bodywork uses the reserved green ramp above.
